text:
RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 3

An all-male panel selecting a man over another man tells you essentially nothing about sex discrimination against you. If anything, the panel's composition cuts against that theory. Raising it would likely read as grasping and undermine your credibility on the point that actually matters.

Your real grievance is substantive: eight years versus fifteen, and a vague "excellent client relationships" criterion that may not have been in the published person specification. That's where to push. Chase the written explanation, in writing, citing your earlier request and its date. Ask specifically how candidates were scored against the advertised criteria and whether client relationships were a stated requirement.

Keep it factual and focused — that's your strongest position.
